_: Measured geometry for the portals drawn on their sheet's own coordinates by shared/plano_svg.js. Every number was READ off the sheet in scripts/ocr — the kerbs and ring by colour (_extract.mjs), the furniture by a dark-column profile of its band (_map.mjs), the labels by their own bounding boxes (_text via _atlas.mjs) — and checked against it with _diff.mjs, which scores the drawing against the sheet region by region. A station that is not in here falls back to the column drawing in shared/plano.js.

TM0029.source: Plano de ubicacion, Portal Norte - Unicervantes, version diciembre de 2025.
TM0029.why: The sheet is 1024x576 and the drawing occupies x 192..1032, y 172..510, so the viewBox is that window of the sheet's own page and a coordinate here is a coordinate there. The turnaround caps are ELLIPSES: at mid-height the ring is only 7px thick on the left (grey at x 211..218), so rxo is 80 against a ry of 92 and rxi 73 against 34. Drawn round they bulged half a platform-width past the sheet at both ends. The outer kerbs are shorter than the inner pair because the troncal stopping zone is shorter than the platform. The furniture x's are each tile's own, not a pitch: Plataforma 2 west runs six tiles at 34px where Plataforma 1 west runs five at 43, and one pitch for both put a tile through the Plataforma 2 tag.

TM0058.source: Plano de ubicacion, Portal 80, version diciembre de 2025.
TM0058.why: NOT a ring. Portal 80 draws two long lozenges lying diagonally, each bending once in the middle, with no turnaround loop anywhere — so it uses `andenes` (a platform as a thick round-capped polyline) where Portal Norte uses `anillo`, and it is drawn WITHOUT an outline: what reads as a platform edge on this sheet is the yellow kerb on the boarding side and bare page on the other. The axes come from the KERBS: both sit at a constant 44.5 off the centre, so sampling them across the whole length and taking the middle gives an axis that is exact everywhere rather than fitted where the sheet happened to be legible — the first attempt was fitted only over the stretch where all four kerbs show at once and came out six pixels adrift at the western end, which then showed up as every bay, caption and tile drifting the same six. Each platform also carries a SPINE: the black line the shelters back onto, with every piece of furniture threaded on it. The bay bar is ONE band per platform from cap to cap, not one per group of bays. Type here is set larger than at Norte — the badges nearly twice the size — so the sizes travel with the station in `tipo`. What the station stands on is drawn too, and all of it UNDER the platforms: the pedestrian tunnel and the evacuation route as walled corridors with dashed edges, the planting, the Centro Comercial and its escalator bank, and Calle 80 ruled and named along itself. The sheet paints the platforms over the corridors, which is why a tunnel edge stops at a kerb and picks up again beyond it rather than being drawn in two pieces.

TM0099.source: Plano de ubicacion, Portal Sur - JFK Coop Financiera, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0099.why: THREE platforms drawn LEVEL and identical: the same rectangle three times, 325 to 822, stacked 108 apart, each with the planting behind it as a round-capped band of the same width — which is why the platform itself is drawn with SQUARE ends and the green with round ones, and why a platform drawn the way Portal 80 draws its own came out 26px too long at each end and swallowed the green. One pedestrian tunnel crosses all three at the same point and lands on the Acceso peatonal block below them. The bays are not cut into a bar here: each is a short bar in the ROUTE OWN COLOUR set beside its name, out on the page under the platform. And the furniture is printed the other way round from the other two portals — a grey glyph on a PALE tile rather than a white one knocked out of black. The bay marks carry the colour the SHEET prints, not the catalog route colour: this plan inks its alimentadores one blue, its zonales one green and its troncal bay orange, and a plano is a snapshot of the operator printing rather than a live view of the catalog.

TM0118.source: Plano de ubicacion, Portal Usme, version julio de 2025, con la redistribucion de plataformas del aviso de TransMilenio vigente desde el sabado 19 de septiembre de 2026.
TM0118.why: TWO platforms drawn LEVEL, the same pale slab twice with a round green end at each side, and the kerb yellow along the TOP edge only. The bays are neither cut into one band nor set beside their names: each is its own grey bar inside the kerb, butted to the next with a hairline, its arrow pointing up at the kerb, and the names stand over them on the page, stacked upward when a bay has two routes. Where the tunnel comes up, a darker mouth is cut into each platform, outlined in ink except where the ramp and the stair open out of it. The entrance is two drums, Planta Alta over Planta Baja, each ruled with the radial treads of a spiral stair, with the access wing off the upper one and a stem down to Plataforma 2. The furniture is white knocked out of black, as at Portal Norte and Portal 80, and the north point is turned: north is to the LEFT on this sheet. From 19 September 2026 the operator redistributed the platforms: the badges, the bay pairings on Plataforma 1, the bay numbers A1-A10 printed on the bars and the "TransMiZonales" captions follow its notice; the geometry is still the July 2025 sheet's, which the notice redraws unchanged.

TM0045.source: Plano de ubicacion, Portal Suba, version mayo de 2025.
TM0045.why: TWO platforms drawn LEVEL, each a slab in two tones — darker north of its spine, paler south of it — with a green half disc at each end. The outer edges are not straight: Plataforma 2's north kerb runs in two long ramps that step back at their ends, and Plataforma 1's south kerb mirrors it, so both slabs are drawn from their measured outline rather than as bands. The bays are Plataforma 2's: nine grey bars along its south edge, each with its arrow pointing down at the kerb and its names on the page below. Plataforma 1 has the two arrival zones, one long bar each. The pedestrian bridge between the platforms is a pale green band, crossed by a pale strip that runs on south to the access building; the building is drawn in its own greys with the ramp, torniquetes, stair, taquilla and TransMiBici where the sheet puts them. The Super CADE beside it is the sheet's D-shaped block.

TM0087.source: Plano de ubicacion, Estacion Portal Americas, version agosto de 2026.
TM0087.why: THREE platforms drawn LEVEL, each a slab with a round end both sides and a south kerb that falls twice and steps back, so each is drawn from its measured outline. Every platform carries its bays along the north edge as grey bars under the kerb, the arrival zones pointing down into the platform and the bays pointing up at the kerb, with the names over them. The pedestrian bridge crosses all three at one point and runs on south to the access building; across the platforms the sheet draws it as a pale VEIL, the bays and kerbs showing paler beneath it rather than painted out. Thin green bands separate the platforms, and the whole station stands in a rounded outline, with the beige ground, the Super CADE, the lawn and the access building to the south. The sheet is published at 1920 by 1080, so these are its own pixels.

TM0145.source: Plano de ubicacion, Portal 20 de Julio, version noviembre de 2024.
TM0145.why: ONE island platform with a green bed capping each end, and both of its kerbs cut as five shallow ramps that step back together at four points — so the slab is drawn from its measured outline rather than as a band. TWO pedestrian bridges cross it and they are what divide its boarding zones: C25 and K10 board the northern edge, route 2, M82, B18 and D81 the southern. The zonal platforms are north of it, drawn as the sheet draws them: Plataforma Norte is the alimentador ARRIVAL area, one long scalloped bar and no bays, and Plataforma Sur carries the eight departure bays, each tagged above with its código and destination. South of the platform the sheet draws the concourse it stands in — the Plazoleta IPES, the Super CADE, the commercial strip and the access hall with its TransMiBici, ramp, stair, torniquetes and taquilla — and the evacuation route running the width of it to Carrera 5a.

TM0135.source: Plano de ubicacion, Portal Eldorado - C.C. NUESTRO BOGOTA, version febrero de 2025.
TM0135.why: ONE long island between the two carriageways of AV. El Dorado, drawn in the sheet's own warm grey rather than the cool grey the other portals use, with the station rooms on it as white boxes and its plant rooms as dark ones. Its boarding points are not bays cut into a bar: each is a coloured DOT on the slab with a line to a rule and the badge hung off it, which is how this sheet names them — K86 and B23 at the west end, B16 and G43 along the north edge, H54, L10, M86 and route 1 along the south. The zonal platforms are separate bars north and south of it, each with its own kerb, and their bays are marked the same way: a square on the bar, a line to a rule, the código and destination under a coloured bar. Both strips end in an alimentador arrivals zone, marked with the sheet's green bus sign. An access block at each end — the western one reached by a ramp off the street, the eastern one by the pedestrian bridge over the avenue. NOT drawn: the C.C. Nuestro Bogotá and Hiper Centro Corora buildings, which the sheet names but leaves blank. Where the sheet and the catalog agree against the stored strip, the strip is corrected: the sheet prints 16-1 Tierra Grata over 16-3 AV. Eldorado Álamos on the fourth northern bay, and the catalog has 16-1 Tierra Grata and 16-3 Álamos, so the bay carries both.

TM0119.source: Plano de ubicacion, Portal Tunal, version junio de 2025.
TM0119.why: TWO platforms that do not lie the same way: Plataforma 1 runs along Avenida Boyacá and Plataforma 2 leaves it at 27 degrees, running down to the TransMiCable station — so its badges, its platform tag, its bay markers AND its bay names all turn with it, which no other portal sheet asks for. Each platform is a boarding strip with a darker bay bar along its outer edge, a kerb on each side, and a zonal arrivals zone at its far end. North of them runs the access concourse with its torniquetes, TransMiBici and taquilla, reached from Avenida Boyacá; two pedestrian TUNNELS land on the platforms, each drawn as the sheet draws it — a diamond with its own furniture. What makes this sheet unlike every other is the south-east corner: the cable station is a disc with a hexagonal hall inside it, the cabin drawn in TransMiCable red on its own angle, planting curved round the outside, and the line itself running off the page to Juan Pablo II, Manitas and Mirador del Paraíso, its three stops drawn as beads on the cable. The plate naming it is the operator's orange rather than the platform yellow, because it names a different system.
